component_records.title: Project management, schedule and MoDOT coordination
component_records.description: A named project manager runs the engagement across the full 15-month contract period, from the 11/15/2024 kick-off to the final invoice on 2/2/2026, with a single integrated schedule that maps every task, deliverable and reporting obligation to those dates. The schedule is baselined at kick-off with MoDOT: kick-off meeting with MoDOT on 11/15/2024, quarterly status meetings reviewing the previous period and anticipated next-period work (in person or online), minutes for the kick-off and every quarterly meeting, and monthly e-mail and phone progress updates to MoDOT contacts. Quarterly updates on work accomplished are submitted on or before the last working day of March, June, September and December so they can feed the SPR Quarterly Report, and an interim presentation is delivered by 9/15/2025. The plan is explicitly subject to MoDOT's ultimate authority to approve work plans, and the Offeror coordinates fully with the Construction and Materials Division and keeps advice and information available to that Division throughout the Agreement, consulting MHTC's representative on any administration concerns. The team also works to the RFP's stated submission deadlines and observes the 7:30 a.m.-4 p.m. Central window for RFP events, with all questions routed only to MoDOTResearchRFP@modot.mo.gov by 7/17/2024 4 p.m. Central. Close-out is planned from the start: the final invoice is prepared and submitted on 2/2/2026 as the last act of the 15-month term, after MoDOT acceptance of the 1/1/2026 final deliverables, so the contract ends on that date with no open work.

component_records.title: Literature review of state DOT AI/ML right-of-way practice
component_records.description: Task 2 delivers a structured literature search and review of how other state DOTs use AI/ML for right-of-way purposes, covering peer-reviewed research, DOT research reports and published practice guidance, with a written review chapter that feeds the Synthesis Report. The review is scoped with MoDOT at kick-off so coverage (states, period, ROW use cases) matches what the Technical Advisory Committee expects, and it establishes the baseline against which the proof-of-concept results are judged. It is scheduled inside the first phase of the 15-month term so its findings inform program selection and the demonstration design.

component_records.title: LLD development program selection and MoDOT IS approval
component_records.description: Before any proof-of-concept work, the team names the program it will use to develop LLDs and submits it to MoDOT Information Systems for approval, including version, hosting model, licensing position, data flows and security documentation so the IS review can proceed without follow-up cycles. No Task 3c demonstration activity starts until that approval is in hand, and the approval package is prepared in parallel with the literature review to protect the 4/25/2025 demonstration date. The selected program is built only on the RFP's approved technologies: .NET 6.0 or above (or a supported .NET Framework 4.8+ where specifically needed), MVC/Razor Pages/Web API, and C#, JavaScript, CSS, HTML and Python, with Python confined to ESRI scripts and small one-time uses unless the IS Best Practices Review Team approves larger use. Any third-party tool that would place a licensing responsibility on MoDOT is submitted to the BRPT and IS management for prior approval, and library dependencies are reviewed and updated annually.

component_records.title: LLD drafting engine configured to MHTC parameters and EPG 236.4.6.2
component_records.description: The core build: a browser-based drafting assistant that ingests the MHTC parameters and source deed/ROW data for a property and generates a first-draft legal land description that ROW staff can review and edit. The drafting rules encode the RFP's substantive requirements - metes-and-bounds descriptions for realty rights acquired or conveyed unless the property is acquired in its entirety, in which case the description reproduces the last deed of record verbatim, and explicit recitation of the specific rights acquired, conveyed or leased where less than fee simple title is conveyed - and every draft is checked against MoDOT Engineering Policy Guide Section 236.4.6.2 before release, with a professional land surveyor reviewing each description before any deed is presented to a grantor. The application is web-based with no client-side software beyond a modern browser, meets WCAG 2.1 AA and the State of Missouri Accessibility Standard based on Section 508, is tested on the latest IS-approved browsers, and stores no PII unless a specific business need is approved by the IS Cyber Security Team. On-premise data sits on Oracle 19C (or the latest supported SQL Server where MoDOT IS Data Service Management approves), and no third-party text, images, code or graphics are used without permission and no vendor branding appears where a licensed option removes it.

component_records.title: Proof-of-concept demonstration on a variety of properties
component_records.description: Task 3c runs the drafting engine across a variety of property types and presents, on 4/25/2025, how the technology creates draft legal land descriptions, with MoDOT ROW staff reviewing the drafts and returning improvement feedback that is logged and dispositioned. The demonstration shows the full path from source data to an editable metes-and-bounds draft, including the acquired-in-entirety case that reproduces the last deed of record, so MoDOT can judge the tool's usefulness on evidence rather than description. Feedback is triaged into tool changes, and the resulting adjustments are the input to the 7/25/2025 manual and training.

component_records.title: Tool refinement, user manual and ROW staff training
component_records.description: After the demonstration feedback is incorporated, the team delivers a user manual and trains MoDOT ROW staff by 7/25/2025, covering how to load property data, generate a first draft, edit it, and route it for surveyor review. Training is delivered in sessions sized and formatted to MoDOT's preference (on-site or virtual) with the manual as the standing reference, and the manual is maintained through the final deliverable so staff have a current document at contract close. Training effectiveness is checked with a short exercise in which staff produce and correct a draft themselves.

component_records.title: Synthesis report, final report, research summary and staff presentation
component_records.description: Task 5 delivers a draft Synthesis Report and Research Summary by 11/3/2025 that are complete final products except for revisions arising from MoDOT's review. Task 6 delivers by 1/1/2026 the final report detailing every task completed and all findings generated during the project, a 1-2 page research summary stating objectives, findings and conclusions, a presentation for MoDOT staff summarizing the significant results, and the final user manual. Reports follow the Publication Guidelines and summary template, and the final report carries a completed Technical Report Documentation page. These deliverables are sequenced to land a month before the 2/2/2026 contract end so MoDOT review, acceptance and the final invoice all fall inside the 15-month term.

component_records.title: Data management plan and data handling
component_records.description: A Data Management Plan is submitted to MoDOT within two weeks of the 11/15/2024 kick-off (12/4/2024), describing the anticipated formats of the project's data and related files and committing to platform-independent, non-proprietary formats so the data and any resulting model artifacts retain future utility for MoDOT. The plan also sets out how source deeds, ROW records and generated drafts are stored, versioned and handed over at close, and confirms that no PII is retained without an approved business need.

component_records.title: Contract, compliance and insurance obligations
component_records.description: A compliance lead owns the non-technical obligations end to end. The Offeror accepts that award is subject to a post-award negotiated contract incorporating the RFP's contract provisions, and that MHTC may cancel the award and select another Offeror if terms cannot be agreed; the Agreement comprises the RFP and its amendments, the proposal and the post-award contract, with MHTC's written clarifications governing conflicts, and any change requires a formal amendment signed by both authorized representatives. The Offeror remains fully liable for the quality and performance of all services regardless of subcontractors, will not assign, delegate or novate without MHTC's prior written consent, and will not release any material or report publicly without MHTC's prior consent. All documents, reports and exhibits produced at MHTC's direction and all information MHTC supplies remain MHTC property, MHTC may reproduce and use derived products without royalties, and working papers and records are retained and made available to MHTC and the Missouri State Auditor at no charge during the term and for three years after final payment. Confidential factual matters supplied by MHTC are not disclosed to third parties except as required by statute, ordinance or court order or as MHTC authorizes, and MHTC is notified immediately of any request for such information. The Offeror complies with Missouri Executive Order 07-13 on employment eligibility, certifies by signature that every assigned employee is authorized to work in the United States, flows Section (3) paragraph I into every subcontract, and takes any action the Commission directs to enforce those provisions including sanctions for noncompliance. The Offeror affirms by sworn affidavit and documentation its enrollment and participation in a federal work authorization program such as E-Verify, provides the E-Verify MOU for proposed staff, affirms it does not knowingly employ unauthorized aliens, and - where the entity is a sole proprietorship or partnership - provides each proprietor's or general partner's affirmative proof of lawful presence under Section 208.009, RSMo, certifying the affidavit facts required by Section 285.530, RSMo. The Offeror carries General Liability of at least $500,000 per person and $3,000,000 per occurrence, Automobile Liability at the same limits, and a Missouri State Workmen's Compensation policy or equivalent, and can furnish certificates before contract signing. Written requests for MHTC/MoDOT help in obtaining citizenship or lawful-presence documentation are submitted in writing, and the Offeror pursues minority and women direct hiring and 10% MBE / 5% WBE subcontracting participation as encouraged.

component_records.title: Cost estimate and price page
component_records.description: The proposal carries a cost estimate covering every service in the Scope of Work, presented on Section (4), Price Page, and signed and returned with the proposal. Costs are broken into Salaries, Benefits, Operating Expense, Facilities and Administration (F&A) Cost, Miscellaneous and Total, with miscellaneous items itemized on an additional sheet where needed, and the whole estimate is held within the $175,000 not-to-exceed amount for the full 15-month period of performance. The estimate is built bottom-up from the milestone schedule so each task, deliverable and reporting obligation is priced once, and it carries the close-out cost of final report acceptance and the 2/2/2026 final invoice so no work falls outside the priced term.

component_records.title: Qualified organization, team and references
component_records.description: The bid is submitted by a qualified organization - a university research unit or research consultancy - with a team pairing land-surveying and ROW practitioners with applied AI/ML engineers, and a documented record of delivering comparable research services in the past three years with at least three named client officials as references. The team's Missouri state-agency and local-government experience is highlighted, and any sub-offerors are listed with complete contact information. The team is staffed for the full 15-month term, with named personnel committed through the 2/2/2026 close-out rather than only through the technical tasks.

items.text: The client is the Missouri Highways and Transportation Commission (MHTC), acting through the Missouri Department of Transportation (MoDOT), with the study coordinated by the Research Unit of the Construction and Materials Division.

MoDOT's Right of Way (ROW) staff currently produce legal land descriptions that must accurately define land areas or rights acquired, conveyed or leased, reciting specific rights where less than fee simple title is conveyed.

Realty rights acquired or conveyed by MHTC must be described by metes and bounds unless the property is acquired in its entirety, in which case the description must be written exactly as it appears on the last deed of record.

Every description prepared for MHTC must meet the requirements of MoDOT Engineering Policy Guide (EPG) Section 236.4.6.2, and a professional land surveyor must review the description before a general warranty deed, quitclaim deed or similar document is presented to the grantor.

The business driver is to determine whether AI and Machine Learning can usefully produce a "first draft" of the legal land description (LLD) using MHTC parameters, reducing the manual drafting burden on ROW staff.
MoDOT's fiscal year runs from July 1 to June 30, and quarterly project updates feed the Statewide Planning and Research (SPR) Quarterly Report the Construction and Materials Division submits to FHWA.

MoDOT wants a research project that determines the usefulness of AI/ML for generating a first draft of legal land descriptions, delivered under a 15-month contract that is estimated to start November 1, 2024 and ends with the final invoice on 2/2/2026.
The Offeror must conduct a literature review of other state DOT practices using AI/ML for right-of-way purposes (Task 2).
The Offeror must name the program it will use to develop LLDs and obtain MoDOT Information Systems approval of that program before any proof-of-concept work begins (Task 3b).

The Offeror must demonstrate, on a variety of properties, how the technology creates draft legal land descriptions, with MoDOT reviewing the drafts and providing improvement feedback (Task 3c), presented to MoDOT on 4/25/2025.
The Offeror must train ROW staff on the finalized tool and supply a user manual (Task 4), with the manual and training delivered by 7/25/2025.

The Offeror must deliver a draft Synthesis Report and Research Summary (Task 5) by 11/3/2025 and a final report, 1-2 page research summary, presentation for MoDOT staff, and user manual (Task 6) by 1/1/2026.

The Offeror must manage the project with a kick-off meeting on 11/15/2024, quarterly status meetings with minutes, monthly e-mail and phone progress updates, and an interim presentation near the project midpoint (due 9/15/2025).
Proposals must be emailed to MoDOTResearchRFP@modot.mo.gov by 10 a.m. Central on August 21, 2024, with receipt notification sent by noon the same day.
All questions and comments must go only to MoDOTResearchRFP@modot.mo.gov by 4 p.m. Central on 7/17/2024, and contacting MoDOT employees by any other method is cause for disqualification.
MoDOT will post its responses to questions publicly on 7/31/2024 and will notify submitters of project selection or interviews on 9/18/2024.

Award goes to the Offeror providing the best proposal, with proposals first screened for responsiveness and then evaluated by a Technical Advisory Committee against criteria the RFP does not list or weight.
The Work Plan must be narrative, limited to ten (10) pages with font no smaller than 12 points, must cover all items in Section 2, and must recognize MoDOT's ultimate authority to approve work plans.

Proposals must be submitted as one combined PDF in a fixed order: Proposal Submission Form, optional one-page cover letter, body of proposal (work plan and schedule), personnel, organization's project experience, team member experience, and client references.
The proposal must show experience delivering the requested services in the past three years and name at least three client officials from the past three years as references.
The Offeror must present a demonstration of AI writing a legal land description and provide training to ROW staff, both of which MoDOT will use to judge the tool's usefulness.

Services under the RFP may not exceed a not-to-exceed amount of $175,000, with costs itemized on the Section (4) Price Page across salaries, benefits, operating expense, facilities and administration, and miscellaneous.

Any application must be built on approved technologies: .NET 6.0 or above (or a supported .NET Framework 4.8+ where specifically needed), web applications using MVC, Razor Pages or Web API, with C#, JavaScript, CSS, HTML and Python as approved languages—Python reserved for ESRI scripts and small one-time uses unless the IS Best Practices Review Team approves larger use.

No third-party tools or software that would place a licensing responsibility on MoDOT may be used without prior review and approval by the Information Systems Best Practices Review Team (BRPT) and IS management.

Applications must be web-based, require no client-side software beyond a modern browser (no Java Applets or Silverlight), and meet WCAG 2.1 AA and the State of Missouri Accessibility Standard based on Section 508.

On-premise databases must run on Oracle 19C or the latest supported SQL Server (SQL Server 2016+ only with MoDOT IS Data Service Management approval), and no personally identifiable information may be stored without a specific business need and IS Cyber Security Team approval.

All documents, reports and exhibits the Offeror produces at MHTC's direction, and all information MHTC supplies, remain MHTC property, and MHTC may reproduce and use derived products without royalties while auditing records for three years after final payment.
The Offeror must submit a Data Management Plan within two weeks after the kick-off meeting (due 12/4/2024) describing data formats and how platform-independent, non-proprietary formats will be used.

The RFP refers bidders to documents not included in it—the Standard Research Agreement, the Publication Guidelines and research summary template, the Proposal Submission Form, and the cost estimate template—all of which must be obtained from https://www.modot.org/information-researchers.
MoDOT's fiscal year runs July 1 to June 30 and quarterly project updates feed the SPR Quarterly Report submitted to FHWA, which sets the quarterly reporting rhythm.
The contract is estimated to start November 1, 2024 and end with the final invoice on 2/2/2026.
The RFP requires the Offeror to name the LLD development program and obtain MoDOT Information Systems approval before proof-of-concept work begins.

MoDOT ROW staff currently produce legal land descriptions that must recite specific rights where less than fee simple title is conveyed, and a professional land surveyor must review each description before a deed is presented to the grantor.
All documents, reports and exhibits the Offeror produces at MHTC's direction, and all information MHTC supplies, remain MHTC property, with records audited for three years after final payment.
Services under the RFP may not exceed a not-to-exceed amount of $175,000, itemized on the Section (4) Price Page.

The MHTC parameters are assumed to be the deed, ROW plan, parcel and title inputs plus the EPG 236.4.6.2 drafting conventions, and the team will confirm the definitive parameter set with MoDOT at kick-off rather than assume a documented specification exists.
EPG Section 236.4.6.2 is assumed to be obtainable from MoDOT's public Engineering Policy Guide in its current edition, and the current edition governs.

The milestone dates in the RFP (kick-off 11/15/2024, DMP 12/4/2024, demonstration 4/25/2025, training 7/25/2025, interim presentation 9/15/2025, draft documents 11/3/2025, final documents 1/1/2026, final invoice 2/2/2026) are treated as binding and are priced as such, with the 15-month term read as ending on the 2/2/2026 final invoice date.
The Data Management Plan is assumed due 12/4/2024, the later of the two stated dates, and is drafted from kick-off so it can be filed earlier if MoDOT prefers.

The proof of concept is assumed to cover roughly six to ten properties spanning whole-take, partial-take and easement acquisitions, with the demonstration delivered as a live walkthrough plus sample draft outputs.
ROW staff training is assumed to be two sessions for up to about twenty staff, delivered virtually with an on-site option, plus the written user manual.
The literature review is assumed to cover all 50 state DOTs' published AI/ML right-of-way work over the past ten years, delivered as a report chapter and a short summary briefing.
The $175,000 cap is assumed to be all-inclusive of labor, travel, overhead and any licensing or hosting costs, with no separate reimbursement.

The Section (4) Price Page and the cost estimate template are assumed to be obtainable from the MoDOT information-for-researchers web page, and the submitted estimate is assumed to be a firm not-to-exceed price refined only by post-award negotiation.

The approved-technologies list in the RFP is assumed to be the complete set, so the solution is designed on .NET 6.0+, MVC/Razor Pages/Web API and C#/JavaScript/CSS/HTML with Python limited to ESRI scripts and small one-time uses.
Oracle 19C is assumed to be the default on-premise database, with SQL Server used only if MoDOT IS Data Service Management approves it.
The insurance limits are assumed to be binding contract requirements at the stated amounts, with certificates available before contract signing.
Confidential factual matters are assumed to be identified by MHTC marking at the time of delivery, and the Offeror will notify MHTC of any disclosure request within one business day.

Working papers and records are assumed to include AI model artifacts, prompts, training data and intermediate draft outputs, all of which will be retained and made available to MHTC and the State Auditor.

The Standard Research Agreement, Publication Guidelines, summary template and Proposal Submission Form are assumed to be obtainable from https://www.modot.org/information-researchers and are reviewed before pricing and before report drafting.
The IS-approved browser list is assumed to be the current MoDOT IS list at time of testing, and the application will be tested against the latest versions on that list.

Exhibits A and B not in the RFP, blocking the worker-eligibility affidavits. The RFP requires a sworn affidavit of non-employment of unauthorized aliens (Exhibit A) and a sworn affidavit of lawful presence for sole proprietors/general partners (Exhibit B), but neither exhibit is included in the PDF. The bid team cannot see the exact affidavit wording, notary and certification fields, or whether a joint venture needs one affidavit per entity, so a proposal can be submitted with a defective or missing affidavit and be ruled non-responsive. If the university or consultancy bids as a partnership, the missing form also delays the pre-signing package. Both exhibits are referenced at p. 15 but absent from the document, and the affidavit obligations are mandatory submission items with disqualification consequences; the bidder has no way to reconstruct the required form.

MoDOT IS approval of the LLD development program gates the 4/25/2025 demonstration. No proof-of-concept work may start until MoDOT Information Systems approves the named LLD development program, but the RFP does not say what the approval package must contain or how long the review takes. The solution plans to prepare the package in parallel with the literature review to protect the 4/25/2025 demonstration date. If IS review runs long or comes back with conditions, the demonstration slips and the whole downstream chain (training 7/25/2025, draft reports 11/3/2025, final 1/1/2026) moves with it. The approval is a hard gate on the critical path with an undefined review duration, and the demonstration date is fixed; a single review cycle of a few weeks would consume the float.

MHTC parameters and EPG 236.4.6.2 are undefined or external. The AI/ML draft must use the MHTC parameters and meet EPG Section 236.4.6.2, but the RFP does not define the parameter set and does not supply the EPG section. The solution assumes the parameters are the deed, ROW plan, parcel and title inputs plus the EPG drafting conventions, and that the current EPG edition governs. If the real parameter set is larger, differently formatted, or the EPG section is not publicly available, the drafting rules must be rebuilt after the price is fixed. The core build depends on inputs the RFP never specifies, and the solution's parameter definition is explicitly an inference; getting it wrong means rework of the central component.

Fixed $175,000 cap against an open-ended research scope. The not-to-exceed amount is $175,000 for a 15-month engagement covering literature review, program approval, a working drafting engine, a demonstration, training, a manual and four report deliverables. The solution assumes the cap is all-inclusive of labour, travel, overhead and any licensing or hosting costs, with no separate reimbursement. Any unplanned IS approval cycle, accessibility remediation or extra property sample comes straight out of margin, and the RFP does not say whether the estimate is binding or refined after award. The cap is fixed and the scope is broad and partly undefined; the solution's own assumption that licensing and hosting sit inside the cap is a material cost exposure on a research budget.

Contract end date conflicts with the 15-month term. The RFP states a 15-month contract period but also fixes the final invoice and contract end at 2/2/2026, which is roughly 14.5 months after the 11/15/2024 kick-off. The proposed solution prices the full 15 months and treats 2/2/2026 as the end, so either the schedule is compressed by about two weeks or the priced effort exceeds the term the client will actually pay for. A late final invoice or a deliverable slipping past 2/2/2026 leaves work outside the contract. The two dates are irreconcilable as written and the solution assumes both are binding, so the mismatch is certain to surface at contract negotiation or at close-out.

Oracle 19C versus SQL Server conflict drives the data layer design. One requirement mandates Oracle 19C for on-premise deployments while another directs the application to run on the latest supported SQL Server, with SQL Server 2016+ only by MoDOT IS approval. The solution assumes Oracle 19C is the default and SQL Server the exception. If MoDOT's IS team expects SQL Server, the data layer, hosting and licensing assumptions change after the price is fixed, and Oracle licensing inside the $175,000 cap is a real cost exposure. The requirements genuinely conflict and the RFP does not say which platform MoDOT's environment runs; the choice affects build effort, licensing and the IS approval package.

Python approval gate before the proof of concept. Python is confined to ESRI scripts and small one-time uses unless the IS Best Practices Review Team approves larger use, and the RFP does not define what counts as large-scale use or how long BRPT review takes. The proposed solution assumes Python stays small. If the drafting engine needs Python for text generation or model work, the team must either re-implement in C# or wait on a BRPT approval that is not on the schedule, adding rework or delay. The solution's own assumption that the approved-technology list is complete and Python stays small is untested; AI/ML work commonly pulls in Python libraries, and the approval path is undefined.

Proof-of-concept scope and training scope unpriced. The RFP does not say how many properties or which property types the demonstration must cover, nor how many ROW staff must be trained, in what format or how many sessions. The solution assumes six to ten properties across whole-take, partial-take and easement acquisitions and two virtual sessions for about twenty staff. If MoDOT expects a larger sample or on-site training across districts, the effort and travel exceed what was priced inside the $175,000 cap. Both scopes are explicitly left open by the RFP and the solution fills them with inferences; the cap leaves little room to absorb a larger demonstration or training programme.

Accessibility and PII obligations on a tool handling deed and ROW records.
